sections.label: The field, in one line
items: AI Engineering = integrating, orchestrating, and operating already-trained AI models (mostly LLMs via API) inside production software, not training models from scratch.

sections.label: Adjacent fields, the fast distinction
items: **Data Scientist**: analyzes data to inform decisions.
**AI Researcher**: pushes what models CAN do, publishes.
**MLOps / AI Infra**: builds/operates the platform models run on.
**AI Engineer (you)**: builds what runs ON TOP of an existing model, reliably.

sections.label: Learn-now priority (in order)
items: Python, Git/GitHub, HTTP/REST/JSON, SQL: all 'need to know now.'
C++/Rust/Go: specialized, only relevant deep in infra/platform work.

sections.label: The production lifecycle
items: IDEA → DATA → MODEL/API → BACKEND → RAG/TOOLS/AGENTS → APPLICATION → EVALUATION → DEPLOYMENT → MONITORING.
An AI engineer's work concentrates from Model/API through Monitoring, not the raw Data or Deployment infrastructure stages.

sections.label: Specialization directions (overlapping, not rigid)
items: AI Application Engineer, LLM/Generative AI Engineer, AI/ML Engineer, AI Integration Engineer, AI Automation Engineer, AI Platform/Infrastructure Engineer, MLOps-oriented roles, AI Product Engineer.

sections.label: What this course teaches vs. doesn't
items: Teaches: Python fundamentals, prompting/structured outputs, context budgeting, RAG, tool use, agents, reliability, evaluation (Python Foundations + Modules 1–8).
Doesn't teach: advanced Python, SQL, deployment/cloud, model training/fine-tuning, production vector-DB ops, a specific vendor's SDK syntax.
